text:
mira: quick heads-up — while bringing up hf/xglm-7b we hit a tokenizer file mismatch: tokenizer.json has special_tokens_map but tokenizer_config.json doesn't, and the fast tokenizer binary is missing. model falls back to slow and we get tokenization drift in evals.

sam: got a repro? is this HF artifact naming or conversion script bug? :thinking:

mira: repro attached below, but short version: hf-convert emitted tokenizer.json + merges/vocab, but tokenizer_config.json lacks 'added_tokens' and 'bos_token' entries. fast tokenizer loader bails with FileNotFoundError on tokenizer.json-fast.json and we silently accept slow.

lucas: paste of the loader trace:
```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/models/xglm-7b/tokenizer.json_fast'
  at token_loader.load_fast_tokenizer (/srv/runtime/token_loader.py:143)
  at token_loader.get_tokenizer (/srv/runtime/token_loader.py:87)
  at model_registry.initialize_model (/srv/runtime/model_init.py:52)
  Caused by: KeyError: 'added_tokens' (in tokenizer_config.json)
```

anya: hm. two issues: (1) convert script sometimes writes 'tokenizer.json' and 'tokenizer_config.json' but the fast tokenizer needs a specific layout (single combined json or an incremental file with _fast suffix). (2) some HF repos put special tokens only in tokenizer.json, others in tokenizer_config.json — our loader expects them in both.

sam: what's the minimal local workaround to get the fast tokenizer back online for dedicated testing?

anya: temporary one-liner to synthesize missing fields and force fast load:
```
python -c "import json,sys
j=json.load(open('tokenizer.json'))
try:
  cfg=json.load(open('tokenizer_config.json'))
except FileNotFoundError:
  cfg={}
for k in ['added_tokens','bos_token','eos_token','unk_token']:
  if k in j and k not in cfg:
    cfg[k]=j[k]
json.dump(cfg,open('tokenizer_config.json','w'))
print('patched')"
```

lucas: that fixed the CI run locally. but note: our eval on a small convo shows 0.7% tokenization mismatch vs gold which translates to 1.2 BLEU-ish drop on the quantized eval — likely the reason we saw a quality regression after quant bring-up.

mira: thanks — we should not rely on manual patches. I'm going to: (A) add heuristic merge in our loader that backfills missing special tokens from tokenizer.json when tokenizer_config.json lacks them, (B) make loader log a WARNING (not silent) when falling back to slow, and (C) add a conversion validation step that fails CI if FAST layout is not produced.

sam: +1. timeline? can we ship loader patch as a small canary so Dedicated doesn't pull bad artifacts?

mira: will open PR in infra/runtime today. plan: small heuristic first (safe), then CI check in next day. canary rollout to eng-dedicated tomorrow.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: PR #4283 -> canary-eng-dedicated. Auto-tests: tokenization-smoke, minimal-eval.

anya: one more thought — some HF tokenizers include inline added_tokens as list-of-dicts (with id, content). our merge must support both shapes. add a quick normalizer fn: flatten dict->list-of-strings.

lucas: noted. I'll add a unit test that converts sample HF repos with the three shapes we saw in the wild.

sam: perfect. also flagging product: potential customer-facing regression (we observed generation mismatch in internal demo).

mira: filed infra/runtime issue 8921 and conversion-tool issue 225. I'll drop links in the PR. thanks all :thumbsup:

lucas: if anyone sees other models with odd token files, drop them here and i'll add to the test corpus.

anya: added a quick diagnostic script to tools/token-diagnose that prints a normalized token map and warns about missing files. use it in onboarding.

mira: milestone: loader heuristic + logging (today), conversion CI check (tomorrow), broader fixes (this week).

sam: sounds good.
